newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: PdVSA Cardon reformer down again, may hit loadings.
newsitem.headline: PdVSA Cardon reformer down again, may hit loadings.

text.p: Petroleos de Venezuela's (PdVSA) 45,000 barrel per day (bpd) reforming unit at its refinery in Cardon was off-line again on Friday after attempts to restart it, according to sources familiar with the plant's operations.
The unit was shut down by the effects of a fire in a related unit on July 28 and was a major factor in PdVSA's decision to declare force majeure on nine August cargoes of gasoline.
It was due to return to full capacity on Friday.
But a company source close to the operations of the refinery said the reformer went down again on Friday and was producing only 90 octane material and at a level well below throughput capacity.

"The reformer went down again because it was not obtaining the octanes. The technicians are arriving tomorrow or Sunday to see what is happening. It will be stopped for another five days and will probably affect next month's (September's) loading programme," he said.
The refinery is a key supplier of so-called reformulated gasoline (RFG) and anti-dumping gasoline to the U.S. market and produces about six 230,000-barrel cargoes per month.
